clue.text: 26 scared to go topless

definitions.note: the answer to 26 across, a noun meaning a rebuke or scolding

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, the first letter of the word for scared

parts.note: scared means fearful

explanation.surface: Someone frightened at the idea of taking their top off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: read it as the solution to 26 across, a word for blame or rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding or telling-off is informally called this, as in getting one from the boss.

clue.text: Edmund died with a burst appendix

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

indicators.note: something burst is broken apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A patient named Edmund died of a ruptured appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appendix' looks medical but means the extra section at the end of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are supplementary material added at the end of a document or book.

clue.text: Crush resistance completely

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
out means completely, as in tired out or out-and-out

explanation.surface: An instruction to stamp out all opposition entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat an enemy decisively and drive them off is to crush them.

clue.text: Fledgling unit backs offer

indicators.note: one piece backs another by standing behind it, so the unit comes after the offer

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer, as in a bid for a contract
a foot is a unit of length

explanation.surface: A newly formed military unit supports a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' suggests support or reversal but simply places the unit after the offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or newcomer to an activity, someone inexperienced, is a fledgling in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Its broadcast leads to chuckles of mirth

definitions.text: Its broadcast leads to chuckles of mirth

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are shuffled
leads are the front letters, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Transmitting it makes audiences laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: a TV comedy whose broadcast leads to laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation comedy is a television genre built to make viewers laugh when shown.

clue.text: Very thin, leaving hospital by right form of transport

indicators.note: by means beside, so the next piece is placed alongside
leaving means going out of, so the hospital letter departs from the word for very thin

parts.note: a hairline crack or line is very thin
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A very thin patient discharged from hospital by the proper means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes H from HAIRLINE to give AIRLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger aeroplane is a means of getting from place to place.

clue.text: Generous, in keeping with Christian's essential character

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the word for in contains the rest

parts.note: home means in, as in staying at home
and means together with
the essential, central letter of Christian is S

explanation.surface: A kind act fitting a Christian's fundamental nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but a synonym (at home); 'keeping' is the container, and 'essential character' is the central letter of Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: A substantial or liberal amount, like a large tip, is described as generous.

clue.text: Delighted by drunken partner losing footing

indicators.note: a drunken walk is unsteady and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the footing is the bottom letter in a down clue, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by a tipsy spouse who slips over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing footing' drops the final R of PARTNER, leaving PARTNE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried away with joy or rapture is a strong form of being delighted.

clue.text: Upset about restricting times I drink to combat ageing

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the turned word encloses the next pieces
about means turned round, so the word for upset is read backwards

parts.note: to rile is to upset or annoy
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: An irritated drinker who keeps knocking back a youth tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal but is a synonym: RILE, written backwards as ELIR, holds XI.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemical potion supposed to prolong life indefinitely is a drink against ageing.

clue.text: Chosen Labour leader getting snubbed for following result

indicators.note: snubbed means turned away and replaced, so the leading letter of Labour gives way to the following abbreviation

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in president-elect

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word

parts.note: FF is the abbreviation for following, as in pages cited

explanation.surface: A newly elected Labour leader is shunned after the result.
explanation.walkthrough: In ELECT, the L (Labour's leader) is replaced by FF.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence or outcome produced by a cause is its result.

clue.text: Send up papers current Conservative government's withholding

indicators.note: withholding means keeping something back inside, so the word for government holds the others

parts.note: rule means government, and the 's here is 'has'
ID is identity papers
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Mocking newspapers for revealing what the Tory government is hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or satirise someone, a parody included, is to send them up.

clue.text: Peasant repaired old axe outside

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the word for axe surrounds the rest

parts.note: a chopper is an axe

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, here in a new order

explanation.surface: A countryman fixing an ancient axe outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' could be read as part of the scene, but it tells the axe word to wrap round the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy, boorish rustic, a yokel in heavy boots, is a scornful term for a peasant.

clue.text: Open University cryptographer admits work revolutionised free speech

parts.note: OU is the UK's Open University

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the cryptographer's name takes in the turned work

parts.note: Alan Turing was the famous British code-breaker of Bletchley Park

indicators.note: revolutionised means turned round, so the word for work is read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An Open University codebreaker's revolutionary work about free expression.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Turing broke German codes at Bletchley Park in the Second World War; 'revolutionised' turns the work round before 'admits' puts it inside his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flood of unrestrained words or emotion is an unchecked, freely flowing kind of speech.

clue.text: Small note fails to reach conclusion

indicators.note: failing to reach the end means the last letter is not reached

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

explanation.surface: A brief message that never gets to its point.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adjective it means miniature or diminutive in size.

clue.text: Try to persuade cheat out of lack of respect

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so the cheat leaves the larger word

parts.note: contempt is a lack of respect
to con is to cheat

explanation.surface: Coaxing a con artist into dropping his disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice or lure someone towards an action is to try to persuade them.

clue.text: Shakespeare's taken short in drunken evening

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened name goes into the word for drunken

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

indicators.note: taken short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Will is Shakespeare's first name; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: The Bard, caught short while tipsy one evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken short' (a British idiom for urgently needing a toilet) trims WILL to WIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The fading light at dusk marks the start of evening.

clue.text: Cockney intent on keeping the peace

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the initial H, so the word is said without it

parts.note: a hoarder is someone set on keeping things

explanation.surface: A Londoner determined to maintain public calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, drop their H's: HOARDER becomes 'OARDER, said the same as the answer in a non-rhotic accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Public order means peace and calm under the law, as in law and order.

clue.text: Men supporting outspoken board member

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits below, so the men come after

parts.note: direct means frank or outspoken
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Staff backing a frank member of the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a company's governing board holds this title.

clue.text: Represent someone who tears coat on wall

definitions.meaning: to depict or portray, as an artist does
one who rends or rips apart
a first coat of plaster or cement applied to a wall

explanation.surface: A painter depicting a man who rips the coat on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to portray, one who rips, and a layer of plaster on brickwork.

clue.text: Assistant removing young woman's coat

indicators.note: removing means taking away, here the outer layer of the word
a coat is the outer layer, so the first and last letters are what goes

parts.note: a maiden is a young woman

explanation.surface: A helper taking a girl's coat off for her.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper or aide-de-camp to an official is an assistant.

clue.text: Bobsleigh that's out of the medals?

definitions.text: Bobsleigh that's out of the medals?

indicators.note: out of means taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A sledge team finishing just off the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a bobsleigh crew placed beyond third misses the medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing in that position is well below the three medal places.

clue.text: Upset when superfluous settlement's blocked by Personnel

parts.note: over means left over, surplus

indicators.note: blocked by means having something stuck inside, so the settlement holds the department

parts.note: a town is a settlement
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Annoyance when a pointless town settlement is blocked by HR.
explanation.definitionFit: A government that has been toppled or defeated has been upset.

clue.text: Painful start after he replaces one from which position?

indicators.note: replaces means takes the place of, so the pronoun goes where the numeral one was

parts.note: a wince is a start or flinch of pain
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sudden twinge after a man takes someone's place.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic question word asks from where, or from which place.

clue.text: Assumed illness dispatching old lady took a long time to go

definitions.text: took a long time to go

indicators.note: dispatching means sending off, so the old lady leaves the word

parts.note: to malinger is to feign illness
ma is a mother, an old lady in slang

explanation.surface: Someone faked sickness and the elderly mother took ages to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying on or dawdling before leaving is taking a long time to go.

clue.text: Striker having time for header or pass

indicators.note: for header means in place of the first letter

parts.note: a picket is a striker at the gate

explanation.surface: A footballer with time to head the ball or pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' is not a footballer but a worker on strike, a PICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket or permit for entry is a pass.

clue.text: Head covering subject, having left college

indicators.note: having left means gone away from, so the college leaves the word

parts.note: a topic is a subject

explanation.surface: A subject after leaving college keeps his head covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi or pith helmet is a sun hat, a covering for the head.

clue.text: Light particle is still radiation in the end

parts.note: a still is a photograph

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A light particle remains radiation, ultimately.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantum of electromagnetic radiation is the particle of light.

clue.text: Blame for breaking compass

indicators.note: breaking means cutting into, so the word for for breaks into the word for compass

parts.note: compass means range or reach
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: Blaming someone for smashing a navigation compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Censure or rebuke is a way of blaming someone.
